The guarantee score is favorable but uncertain because the short cross-continuity reference does not establish one explicit universal entitlement. This record deliberately narrows the broad Krypton lead instead of averaging every incompatible version.

Organic councils and institutions retain productive authority, so robot capability does not by itself establish autonomous AI sovereignty. A moderate nonworking estimate allows substantial technical support while counting science, care, administration and other useful chosen careers. Kryptonians are a disclosed humanoid comparison population, not unmarked humans. The planet’s eventual destruction does not make its former residents leisure citizens, and no modern film, television version or later reboot is automatically assigned this material model. Every numeric implication remains a bounded editorial best guess.

after.description:
DC One Million depicts a future Solar System with extraordinary planetary engineering, artificial entities and radically developed human-derived life. The best-guess material reading is a broadly supported civilization in which automated systems reduce the need for subsistence labor. This is an inferred admission rather than a claim that a superhero crossover supplies complete food and housing law. Guarantees are estimated as strong in ordinary life, with wide uncertainty about local conditions and exclusions.

Control is placed toward shared human-derived civilization, while allowing major concentrated institutions and powerful artificial agents. The mere existence of a heroic team or a hostile Solaris does not establish who owns every productive system. A high nonworking estimate reflects technical abundance but retains research, care, maintenance, governance and other useful activity. Human-derived persons remain the declared denominator; not every robot, cosmic entity or inactive archive is counted as a human nonworker. Crisis destruction and rival futures are outside this provisional point.
